Scope: infrastructure networks over about 3.5 km² in Zones A and B and the Labour Community Area, around 100 km south-east of Riyadh.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. Against the revised plan issued on 26 Oct, the project is 0.6% ahead: 50.4% complete against 49.8% planned, after gaining 1.2% this week against 0.75% planned.

The finish date is back on the contract date, but the road and MV milestones are three to four months late. The P6 update uploaded this week (data date 03-Nov-2026) finishes the project on 02-Dec-2027 with zero float, against 27-Apr-2028 in last week's file. Road works are forecast for 02-Jan-2027 and the MV network for 08-Feb-2027, 92 and 129 days after their baseline dates, and asphalt works now face a stoppage because of bitumen supply constraints. Against the original baseline, which called for 83.0% by the end of October, the project remains far behind at 50.4%.

The P6 telecom date conflicts with the weekly report's "All networks" forecast of 29-Mar-2027. P6 finishes the telecom network on 26-May-2027 with −95 days of float. Open activities with negative float fell from 1,243 to 574, led by bituminous construction (20), aggregate base course (19) and earthworks (17). The worst float, −110 days, sits on the MV works and on the asphalt binder and base course chain. Last week's file finished the project on 27-Apr-2028; the contractor should explain the logic and duration changes behind the 147-day recovery.

Data notes

  • No progress presentation was uploaded with the 02-Nov report, so quantities by network and zone, and this week's installed quantities, are not available. The scope section uses the weekly report's four-item quantity tracker.
  • The P6 finish moved from 27-Apr-2028 to 02-Dec-2027 in one update, the potable water float from −230 to −46 days and the open negative-float activities from 1,243 to 574. Several in-progress street lighting and curbstone activities still run to 09-Oct-2028, after the project finish, which points to open-ended logic.
  • The main summary sheet shows the milestone forecasts as the baseline dates, while its own days-change column and the Milestones sheet give −92, −129 and −55 days. The consultant's comment sheet at the front of the PDF raises the same point.
  • The cumulative plan rose from 48.4% to 49.8% this week, while the effort table gives 0.75% as this week's planned progress.
  • The manpower plan was replaced (October 677 → 685, November 841 → 721), and the actual October figure of 529 is repeated for the third report with no November count.
  • The weekly report now measures cost against 267,731,582 SAR excluding VAT instead of 307,891,320 SAR, so invoiced to date reads 18.6% instead of 16.1%; the Invoice Log still uses the old value. "Penalties & retention" in the summary now shows 111,000 only, without the 4,971,066 retention.
  • Quality: approved MIRs show 5 cumulative (49 last week), so the counter was reset again; cumulative shop drawings read 20,887 instead of 2,087; NCRs this week are 5 in Quality-Stat but 4 in Weekly Quality. The Quality-Stat sheet also reports cost-based progress as "actual"; it is not used here.
  • The summary panel's FIR counts (353 issued, 294 closed) repeat last week's figures; the Weekly Quality sheet gives 407 FIRs received this week.
  • Procurement notes still say several items finish delivery on 20 Oct (storm manholes, box culverts, sluice valves, MV cable) although they are incomplete, and interlock deliveries rose although supply is recorded as on hold.
  • The SPI sheet labels the new week "Week 5 26.Oct.2026" again, and the HSE "this month" man-hours (131,580) still include October.
